headline: Earnings grow year over year despite softer revenue
summary_short: Ameren's diluted EPS rose to $1.13 in Q2 2026 (+11.9% y/y) as net income attributable to common shareholders grew to $314 million, even though total revenue slipped 5.8% y/y to $2,092 million on much lower off-system power sales; the company reaffirmed full-year guidance of $5.25-$5.45 per diluted share.
summary_long: Second-quarter earnings rose to $314 million ($1.13 diluted EPS, +11.9% y/y) as infrastructure investment across Ameren Missouri, Ameren Transmission, and Ameren Illinois Electric Distribution added earnings, partly offset by higher operations-and-maintenance spending on reliability-focused tree trimming and energy-center maintenance; a higher diluted share count also tempered per-share growth. Total revenue fell 5.8% y/y to $2,092 million as off-system electricity sales dropped to $148 million from $471 million a year earlier. Six-month capital expenditures reached $2,653 million, funded in part by $1,794 million of new long-term debt issuance, lifting long-term debt to $19,064 million and shareholders' equity to $13,687 million. Ameren reaffirmed its full-year 2026 EPS guidance range of $5.25-$5.45.

drivers.explanation: Off-system electricity sales at Ameren Missouri fell to $148M from $471M y/y, a $323M drop that more than explains the $129M net revenue decline -- every other reported revenue line (retail electric, both Illinois segments, natural gas) rose y/y.

Earnings gains from infrastructure investment across all four segments were partially offset by higher operations-and-maintenance expense, mainly increased reliability-focused tree trimming and energy-center maintenance.
The release states the EPS comparison also reflects higher weighted-average diluted shares outstanding in Q2 2026, which tempered per-share growth relative to the net-income increase.
Not detailed for the quarter specifically, but six-month cash flows show $1,794M of new long-term debt issuance funding a $2,653M capital program, consistent with the y/y debt growth.

By segment, Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025 earnings: Missouri $157M vs $150M, Transmission $96M vs $86M, Illinois Electric Distribution $70M vs $64M, Illinois Natural Gas $9M vs $10M, Parent loss narrowed to $18M from $35M. Company reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $5.25 to $5.45 per diluted share.
